To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a synergistic functional network of DEmiRNA and their target genes may be involved in CIN and CSCC.

we have identified a total of four hub genes (TYMS, CDK1, SASH1and AURKA) that are regulated by hsa-miR-21 and hsa-miRR-99a, and may be involved in pathogenesis of CINI and progression of CIN to CSCC.

a total of six biomarkers (four DEGs and two DEmRNAs) may be involved and may serve as novel and noninvasively detectable biomarkers in CSCC, with potential application as diagnostic biomarkers in cervical cancer screening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of miRNA‐messenger RNA (mRNA) functional synergistic networks as a novel diagnostic biomarker for CIN and CSCC.
the potential of hsa‐mir‐99a and hsa‐mir21 as biomarkers for CIN or CSCC, and of TYMS and SASH1 as targets for CSCC treatment.
the synergistic effects of DEmiRNA and DEGs in the development of CSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hsa‐miRNA‐21‐SASH1 and hsa‐mir‐99a‐TYMS regulatory networks are involved in the pathophysiology of cervical cancer.

the synergistic effect of the four DEGs (SASH1, CDKN1B, TYMS, and AURKA), and the two DEmiRNA (hsa‐mir‐99a, hsa‐mir‐21) may be involved the pathogenesis and the progression of cervical squamous cell cancer.
the hsa‐miRNA‐99a/TYMS and the hsa‐mir‐21/SASH1 synergistic network may be a novel biomarker for the early diagnosis of CIN and CSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hsa‐miRNAs‐21 and 99a may be used as novel diagnostic biomarkers of CSCC.
the miRNA‐messenger RNA functional synergistic network of hsa‐mir‐21‐SASH1‐p53 and hsa‐mir-99a‐TYMS‐CDK1 may be involved in cervical tumorigenesis.
hsa‐miRNA‐21 and hasa‐miR‐ 99a could be potential biomarkers of CSCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified a miRNA‐target gene synergistic network for CSCC.
a miRNA‐target gene synergistic network can be used to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets in CSCC.
a synergistic network between DEmiRNA and DEGs may be used for the prediction of CSCC.
